title: DRVS — search that dims instead of replacing
description: A corpus-agnostic, mostly client-side search engine. Instead of replacing your page with a result list, it dims what doesn't match and tells you why what's left is there. MIT.
ogDescription: Reverse semantic masking: your list stays put, the misses fade, and every hit says what actually matched.

hero.h1:
Most search
replaces the page.
This one develops it.
hero.lede: Your list stays exactly where it is, in its own order. A query only changes how visible each row is — strong matches stay lit, weak ones dim, misses fade to a ghost. Nothing is moved, re-sorted, or removed. You keep the context that a results page throws away.

demo.h2: Try it on a real index
demo.intro: Nine documents about entirely mundane things — coffee, balcony tomatoes, a bike chain — deliberately unrelated to anything DRVS was extracted from. This is the actual package running in your browser against a real prebuilt index. Not a mockup, not a recording.
demo.noscript: JavaScript is off, so the search layer isn't running — and the nine documents below are all still here, fully readable. That is the design, not a fallback: the reveal layer is additive, and nothing it does is required to read the page.
demo.corpusFoot: This corpus also exists in Traditional Chinese, with the same ids and the same relations. Both are built and tested the same way — that parallel is how the claim "not script-specific" gets checked instead of asserted.
demo.semanticOff: Enable semantic channel (~25MB model, downloads once)
demo.semanticOn: Semantic channel on — click to disable

tiers.h2: Four tiers, and a floor you can see
tiers.intro: A photographer checks an exposure against a step wedge — a strip of known, evenly-spaced densities. DRVS ranks the same way: every result lands on a fixed step, and the step is the opacity you actually see. These are the real numbers from config/search.config.json, not an illustration.

steps.d: Exact. The query is literally in the title, a heading, or a confirmed alias.
Close. Strong lexical overlap, or an exact hit somewhere less central.
Weak. Character-level or embedding similarity, with no literal anchor.
Distant. Usually structural — a sibling of something that did match.
Masked. Still on the page, still readable, just out of the way.

tiers.note: Tier is never carried by color alone. Each row gets an opacity step and a text label naming the reason, plus data-drvs-tier for assistive tech. In forced-colors mode the opacity ladder flattens and the labels carry it on their own.

channels.h2: A hit reason must name what actually matched
channels.intro: Not a relevance score. Not "the model thinks so." Every result carries a specific claim you can check — and if a channel has nothing to say about a document, it stays silent rather than inventing a number.

cards.p: Substring against title, headings, summary, keywords. Always outranks everything below it.
CJK bigrams and Latin token overlap, so typos and paraphrases still land. No stemmer, no language config.
Alias expansion from evidence you can point at — a curated set, or an acronym a document defines in its own title.
A document with no direct hit can ride in on a curated link to one that did — and it says so, rather than pretending it matched.
cards.c: same series as a confirmed match

cards.p: Embeddings compared in the browser against prebuilt vectors. No API, no per-query cost. Chunk-level, so it can name the passage.
Every optional channel degrades structurally. No dictionary, no vectors, model won't load — the rest keeps working and nothing upstream notices.

principles.eyebrow: The part most search UIs get wrong
principles.h2: Never return zero results without saying so
principles.doP: When nothing clears the confidence bar, it relaxes the threshold, still returns the closest documents, and tells you plainly that it did: "No high-confidence direct match. Showing the semantically closest documents only." You can see the results and you can see the caveat.
principles.dontP: Dress a weak match up as a confident one. Relaxing the threshold is always disclosed, a low-confidence banner is never suppressed, and an index with genuinely nothing in it says so rather than padding the list. Non-zero results is not permission to fabricate.

install.h2: Point it at a list you already have
install.step1p: Python, build time. The helpers do the file-level work — frontmatter, headings, summary, keywords — so your adapter is mostly plumbing.
install.step2p: The control markup is built for you. Your rows are left alone except for classes and data attributes.
install.step3p: Override custom properties. You should never need to fork the stylesheet.
install.honestH3: What you still have to build yourself
install.honestP1: The adapter that turns your actual files into documents — walking your storage, assigning stable ids, mapping URLs. DRVS deliberately has no opinion on what a corpus is made of, because that is the one part no generic package can do for you honestly.
install.honestP2: And what goes in the dictionary. The builder will propose entries from self-defining titles, but a fabricated alias is the most damaging thing this system can do: it makes unrelated documents look like confirmed matches, under the most authoritative label the interface has. Read audit_candidates() output before shipping one.

footer.note: Distilled from a production deployment over a ~2,000-document corpus, then re-verified against a corpus with nothing in common with it.

docPage.extractedH2: What DRVS extracted from this document
docPage.extractedIntro: This is the whole record the search index holds for this page — produced by build/extract.py at build time. Every derived field is tagged with where it came from, so a heuristic guess is never presented as something the author asserted.
docPage.relatedIntro: Declared in the index, not inferred from similarity. A query matching one of these can surface this document through the relation channel — labeled as a relation, never disguised as a direct hit.
docPage.corpusNote: part of the DRVS demo corpus
docPage.footNote: This document is part of a small synthetic corpus written to demonstrate the package on subject matter it has nothing to do with.
